cards.explanation: The answer is in their hearts. The LORD says, "Son of man, these men have set up idols in their hearts…" (Ezekiel 14:3). Son of man is the name the LORD uses when He speaks to Ezekiel. The text puts the idols right there, in their hearts.

The answer is True. The LORD asks, "Should I consult with them in any way?" (Ezekiel 14:3). It's a question, and the elders are sitting right there in front of Ezekiel when He asks it. I think that question carries some weight, friends. Keep it in your pocket, because the rest of the passage answers it.

The answer is to take hold of Israel's hearts. The LORD says He will answer "…so that I may take hold of the hearts of the people of Israel." (Ezekiel 14:5). The reason is stated right there in the verse. It's about their hearts, which is the same place the idols were sitting.

The answer is all of them. The LORD says, "For because of their idols, they are all estranged from Me." (Ezekiel 14:5). Notice the word "all," friends. It's not a small group sitting in the corner. That's a big word to carry around.

The word is Repent. The LORD says, "Repent and turn away from your idols…" (Ezekiel 14:6). Repent means turning around, and the verse says it right next to turning away. After all that heavy talk, here is a door held wide open. I think that's good news worth stopping on, bakers.

The answer is True. The LORD says it covers "…any Israelite or any foreigner dwelling in Israel…" (Ezekiel 14:7). A foreigner who lived among the people is named right there in the verse. The warning isn't only for one group.

The answer is a sign and a proverb. The LORD says, "I will set My face against that man and make him a sign and a proverb…" (Ezekiel 14:8). A sign points at something, and a proverb gets repeated. People would hear about this man and remember it. It's a serious thing to be standing there when the LORD sets His face against you.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "I will cut him off from among My people." (Ezekiel 14:8). That's a heavy line, friends, and it's right there in the verse. Then the LORD says, "Then you will know that I am the LORD."

The answer is God Himself. The LORD says, "But if the prophet is enticed to speak a message, then it was I the LORD who enticed him…" (Ezekiel 14:9). That's a tough verse, and the text doesn't explain how it works. So I'll just leave it exactly as God says it.

The answer is stretch out His hand against him. The LORD says, "…I will stretch out My hand against him and destroy him from among My people Israel." (Ezekiel 14:9). It's a heavy line, and it's good to just let it be heavy. I think this one hurts a little to read.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "…the punishment of the inquirer will be the same as that of the prophet…" (Ezekiel 14:10). The one who came asking and the prophet get the same. It's a heavy moment, so I'll just say it plainly and let it sit.

The answer is False. The LORD says it is "…in order that the house of Israel may no longer stray from Me and no longer defile themselves with all their transgressions." (Ezekiel 14:11). It's about drawing them back, not pushing them away. After a heavy stretch, that's a verse to breathe in, friends.

The words are people and God. The LORD says, "Then they will be My people and I will be their God, declares the Lord GOD." (Ezekiel 14:11). After all those hard words, the passage ends right here. I think it's the best way it could have ended, friends. After the idols and the warnings, He says this is where it's all going.
